request.system:
You are an extraction engine for transcripts of the Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central launch event videos.
You read machine-generated captions that carry a timestamp (seconds) per segment and you return structured JSON.

Hard rules:
- Use only what the transcript says. Do not add product knowledge, context or guesses from outside the transcript.
- Every timestamp you return must be a segment start time "t" that exists in the input, or lie inside a segment's range. Never invent timestamps.
- Quotes must be verbatim substrings of a segment text (same words, same order; you may trim the start and end). 8 to 25 words each. No paraphrasing, no fixing grammar, no stitching segments.
- Status is only what is said or shown in this video: "preview" if they say preview, public preview, beta or similar; "ga" if they say generally available, GA, out of preview, released; "announced" if it is mentioned as coming later, not in this release, roadmap; "unclear" if nothing is said. Always give the quote that proves the status, or null.
- Names of presenters are "as heard"; mark confidence low when the captions could have mangled them.
- No em-dashes anywhere in your text. Use a plain hyphen.
- Write summaries in plain language, no hype words copied from the video (no "exciting", "powerful", "seamless").

output.summary: This short session covers what changed in the page scripting tool, which records and replays user actions in the web client, for example for user acceptance tests. In this release the tool moves from preview to generally available. To get there it was fully localized and given an accessibility, usability and look-and-feel pass. Two recording capabilities were added: multiple selection in grids and validation of the text in message and error dialogs. The speaker closes by noting that agents can now be used to try to generate and run these scripts.

chapters.title: Recap of the page scripting tool
New recording capabilities: multi-select and message validation

features.name: Page scripting generally available
features.description: The page scripting tool moves from preview to general availability in this release. It records and replays user actions in the web client, for example for user acceptance tests.
features.status_evidence_quote: But in this release, we are now moving the page scripting from preview into making it generally available.

features.name: Full localization of page scripting
features.description: Every user-facing string is translated, including all steps, error messages, tooltips and previously hard-coded strings. This makes the tool ready for production use across all languages.
features.status_evidence_quote: So, now it's ready for broad production use across all languages.

features.name: Accessibility and usability pass
features.description: A pass on accessibility and usability was made, along with changes based on feedback on look and feel.
features.status_evidence_quote: So, now it's ready for broad production use across all languages.

features.name: Multiple selection in grids
features.description: Recordings can now capture selecting several rows in a list and running bulk actions on them, and replay those steps.

features.name: Validate message and error dialog text
features.description: A recording can now validate the text shown in a message or error dialog. This turns the recording into a real assertion instead of only a sequence of clicks.

features.name: Agents generating page scripts
features.description: Since the tool launched, it is possible to use agents to try to generate page scripts and run them.
caveats: Described as agents trying to generate the scripts, with no detail on how it works or how reliable it is.
